note: STD-538: node forms of refinement row expressions (history read, whole-population value, seq) over the concrete model acme/counter (object type Counter, population counters, history `history Counter.seen: Int[0, 9] = 0`). Every key is the JCS SHA-256 of the node preimage recorded beside it: structural nodes by quire.structural-node/v1, application nodes by quire.application-node/v1. catalog_delta is the exact change to the checked operation catalog these forms need.

vectors.summary: A history read: `seen` of `Counter` read at the receiver `self`.
The pre-state of that history field, `pre(seen)`, over the history read.
The whole-population value `counters`: all_instances over the population reference, bounded [0, 3].
`count(x in counters)`: count over the population value, binder body the literal true, result Int[0, 3].
`only(x in counters: x)`: only over the population value, binder body the binder, result Reference<Counter>.
`seq(i in 0 .. 3: i)`: seq over two bounded literals, result Sequence<Int[0, 3]>[0, 4].

refusal_cases.summary: A history read names a history the refinement does not declare.
The result type of a history read is not the declared type of the history field.
A history read no refinement row reaches is outside any refinement.
The receiver of a history read is not a reference to the declaring type.
A seq bound whose type is not a bounded integer range has no derived length.
The result bound of a seq is not max(0, hi_max - lo_min + 1).
A population value in a refinement row has no bound.
The member of an only is not the type of its binder bound.
The member declaration of a seq is not the element type of its sequence result (the over_element clause), here the Boolean node against the Int[0, 3] element.
